takeaway: The radial nerve (C5-T1) supplies supinator, extensor carpi ulnaris, brachioradialis and anconeus: all of the above.

question.text: Which of the following muscles are supplied by the radial nerve: supinator, extensor carpi ulnaris, brachioradialis?

lines.text: The radial nerve, C5–T1, supplies the extensor muscles of the arm and forearm.
lines.say: The radial nerve, C five to T one, supplies the extensor muscles of the arm and forearm.

lines.text: The supinator is one of its muscles, and it is the main supinator when the elbow is extended.
Extensor carpi ulnaris extends the wrist, so it is radial nerve too.
Brachioradialis looks like a flexor, but surprise: it is also supplied by the radial nerve.
lines.say: (laugh) Brachioradialis looks like a flexor, but surprise: it is also supplied by the radial nerve.

lines.text: Anconeus joins in as well, a small muscle that straightens the elbow.
So the answer is all of the above.
